name: Paroxysmal Nonkinesigenic Dyskinesia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Paroxysmal Nonkinesigenic Dyskinesia

criteria.description: Recurrent episodes of involuntary dystonia, chorea, or athetosis lasting minutes to hours
Episodes not triggered by sudden voluntary movement but may be precipitated by stress, alcohol, caffeine, or fatigue
Neurological examination is normal between episodes
Positive family history of similar episodes supports diagnosis
Exclusion of secondary causes such as metabolic, structural, or epileptic disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent spontaneous episodes of involuntary movements not triggered by sudden movement, normal neurological exam between episodes, and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for mutations in the PNKD gene can support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.notes: Episodes occur without sudden movement triggers

pathognomonic.symptomName: Prolonged involuntary movement episodes lasting minutes to hours

common.symptomName: Precipitation of attacks by alcohol consumption
Precipitation of attacks by caffeine intake
searchTerms: episodes precipitated by coffee or tea

occasional.symptomName: Aura or prodromal symptoms preceding attacks
Fatigue as a trigger for episodes

rare.symptomName: Autonomic symptoms such as sweating or palpitations during attacks
searchTerms: autonomic symptoms like fast heartbeat and sweating
sympathetic nervous system signs during episodes

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; metabolic panels to exclude secondary causes
imaging: Normal brain MRI; used to exclude structural lesions
genetic: Mutations in the PNKD gene (formerly MR-1) associated with familial cases
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) normal during attacks, helps exclude epileptic seizures

distinguishingFeatures: Attacks triggered by sudden voluntary movements
Shorter duration of episodes (seconds to minutes)
Responds well to anticonvulsants like carbamazepine
Episodes not typically prolonged dystonic/choreoathetoid movements

redFlags: Presence of seizures with loss of consciousness
references: Klebe S, et al. Paroxysmal Nonkinesigenic Dyskinesia: Clinical Features and Genetic Findings. Mov Disord. 2012.
Bhatia KP, et al. The clinical spectrum of paroxysmal dyskinesias. Brain. 1999.
